sections.text: When crumbling driveways, deteriorating patio slabs, or damaged foundation work need to come out, concrete removal Spokane property owners and contractors turn to Northwest Concrete Cutting for professional results. We deliver concrete removal Spokane-wide, serving residential homeowners, commercial clients, and municipal projects across Eastern Washington and Northern Idaho. From a single driveway to a full parking lot tearout, our team handles every phase — breaking, loading, hauling, and site cleanup — so your next project can start on solid ground.
Why Professional Equipment Makes the Difference

Concrete removal is not a job for hand tools and rental breakers. Standard residential slabs weigh between 85 and 150 pounds per cubic foot, meaning a typical two-car driveway contains 6,000 to 8,000 pounds of material. Commercial slabs — especially warehouse floors and parking lots — can easily exceed 50,000 pounds on a single job. Our crews use hydraulic breakers, diamond blade slab saws, skid-steer loaders, and high-capacity dump trucks to work efficiently and safely. Many concrete removal Spokane projects require cutting before breaking — scoring control joints or sectioning large slabs so pieces can be lifted without damaging adjacent structures. Our {{link:/services/concrete-cutting|concrete cutting services}} are routinely integrated into the removal process to keep projects on schedule. Rebar-reinforced slabs add another layer of complexity: the steel must be cut and separated before hauling, which requires both the right saw blades and a clear worksite safety plan. Attempting this work without proper machinery creates real hazards — broken underground utilities, cracked neighboring structures, and serious injury risk for untrained workers. The cost professional concrete removal contractors charge is almost always recovered through speed, safety, and avoiding the expense of preventable mistakes.
How Spokane's Freeze-Thaw Climate Accelerates Concrete Damage

Spokane's high desert climate is uniquely punishing for concrete. Temperatures can swing from well below freezing in December and January to over 100 degrees Fahrenheit in late July, subjecting slabs to extreme thermal expansion and contraction. More damaging are the freeze-thaw cycles that occur dozens of times each winter — water infiltrates micro-cracks in concrete, expands by approximately 9% when it freezes, and forcibly widens those cracks through repeated cycling. Add deicing salt damage and the heavy vehicle loads typical of Eastern Washington winters, and it becomes clear why concrete removal Spokane contractors handle more deteriorated slabs per season than crews in milder climates. The spalling, heaving, and cracking that result from Spokane winters typically affect the upper one to two inches of a slab first, but left unaddressed, damage works deeper and accelerates with each subsequent winter. By the time most homeowners in Spokane Valley, Liberty Lake, and Cheney finally call for service, the slab is compromised through most of its depth. Replacement always starts with thorough removal — patching over damaged concrete or overlaying it traps moisture and shortens the life of any new material placed on top. Our concrete removal Spokane team clears all deteriorated material to a clean subgrade before any new pour begins.
Residential Concrete Removal: Driveways, Patios & Slabs

Residential projects make up the majority of our workload each season. The most frequent calls are for driveway removal, garage slab removal, patio removal, and sidewalk sections heaved by tree root growth. A standard two-car driveway in Spokane generates 3 to 5 cubic yards of concrete debris — material we haul to a regional recycling facility rather than sending to a landfill. Our residential crews use compact equipment that fits through standard fence gate openings, protecting landscaping and hardscaping throughout the job. We mark all underground utilities — gas lines, water service, electrical conduit, and irrigation systems — before breaking begins, every time. For projects that combine demolition with structural work, we coordinate concrete removal with {{link:/services/wall-sawing|wall sawing services}} to eliminate scheduling gaps between phases. Steps, curbs, porch slabs, and post footings are all within our scope. If you're preparing for a new garage build, resurfacing a patio, or removing a deteriorated slab before listing your home, concrete removal Spokane residential customers can schedule a free on-site estimate seven days a week. We also handle targeted partial removals — a single heaved sidewalk panel, an isolated footing, or a partial driveway section — not just full tearouts.
Commercial Concrete Removal for Parking Lots & Industrial Floors

Commercial concrete removal Spokane projects require heavier equipment, larger crews, and more detailed pre-project planning than residential work. We regularly handle parking lot tearouts, warehouse and distribution center floor removal, loading dock apron replacement, retaining wall demolition, curb-and-gutter removal for road improvement projects, and foundation slab work for new commercial construction. Thick commercial slabs — often 6 to 8 inches of reinforced concrete — demand multiple passes with hydraulic breakers before material is small enough to load efficiently. Post-tensioned slabs, common in parking structures and some commercial floors, require {{link:/services/concrete-scanning|ground-penetrating radar scanning}} before any cutting begins to locate tensioned cables and prevent dangerous snap-back incidents. Our commercial division operates with full general liability insurance, workers' compensation coverage, and OSHA safety compliance on every job site. We have completed large-scale concrete removal Spokane projects for industrial tenants in the West Plains corridor, retail developments in Spokane Valley, and municipal infrastructure work in Cheney and Airway Heights. Our high-capacity fleet — tracked excavators and articulated dump trucks — allows us to remove thousands of square feet per shift, keeping commercial timelines intact regardless of slab size or reinforcement type.
What the Concrete Removal Process Looks Like

Every project starts with a site assessment and written estimate. During the walkthrough, we measure the area, probe slab thickness, check for rebar or post-tension reinforcement, identify access constraints, and confirm utility locations. For {{link:/areas/spokane-wa|residential and commercial clients in Spokane, WA}}, most residential jobs wrap up in a single day — a 1,200-square-foot driveway typically takes four to six hours from first break to final load out. Commercial jobs are phased based on site access requirements, tenant operations, and material volume. On the day of work, our crew arrives with all required equipment on the first trip — no waiting on deliveries or last-minute rentals. After removal, we leave the site clear of concrete debris with the subgrade disturbed only as specified in the project scope. We provide final-grade recommendations for upcoming pours and coordinate with your concrete contractor on subgrade compaction requirements. All broken concrete from {{link:/areas/spokane-wa/concrete-removal|concrete removal Spokane projects}} we complete is hauled to a regional recycling facility, diverting material from local landfills and often reducing your net project cost. If you want to understand what concrete removal Spokane pricing looks like for your specific scope, a free site visit is the most accurate path to a firm number.

We also cover Coeur d'Alene and Post Falls in North Idaho, Pullman and the Palouse region to the south, and Columbia Basin communities including Moses Lake, Pasco, Kennewick, and Richland. There's no subcontracting on our jobs — the crew that comes to your estimate is the crew that completes your project.
